precepts.text: Unrighteous men oppress the holy nation, prisoners of darkness exiled from the eternal providence. That has been us this whole time.
precepts.point: Robbed, as Deuteronomy 28:33 says: in Papua New Guinea the tribes of Naphtali and Benjamin export 98 percent of their resources to Australia and Britain, then have to import them back and pay interest. That is being dominated.

precepts.text: Fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false: the athlete making millions running up and down the court thinks he has made it, but the real soul knows he is still a slave. Kaepernick caught the fever and stood up, and they made an example of him; his teammates know he was right and pretend to be fine. That pretence is fear. We cannot drown out the squeaking of our wretched condition with frolic, drugs, alcohol, or music, dancing slaves made to look whole while the spirit rots.
precepts.point: The squeaky wheel gets the oil. We will complain, judge, bring out the records, and beg the Lord until he kills our enemies and sets us up, like the widow before the unjust judge. Our enemies want us silent, locked away with our mouths zipped, calling us troublemakers; yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. Nehemiah 2:10 shows they grieve when a man comes to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

precepts.text: So then whosoever there fell down was straitway kept shut up in a prison without iron bars. Now this is about ancient Egypt, but watch what it says about the Egyptians, and how it relates to us. Just like the ancient Egyptians were in that sea of darkness, it says they were shut up in a prison without iron bars. That is what we are in today. There are no iron bars, and people say, I am free, there are no shackles on me. It is the same thing.
precepts.point: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. You have Christians talking about, did he go under the ground? No. We are in a prison house. Being dominated by another race is a prison. Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and he preached to us.
precepts.why:
Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. Christians ask, did he go under the ground? No. Being dominated by another race is a prison, and Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and preached to us.

Wisdom shows what kind of prison it is. This is about ancient Egypt, but watch what it says about the Egyptians and how it relates to us: “So then whosoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars”. Just like the ancient Egyptians in that sea of darkness were shut up in a prison without iron bars, that is what we are in today. There are no iron bars, so people say, I'm free, there are no shackles on me. It is the same thing.

Isaiah said we are “hid in prison houses”, and those prison houses are democracy, Republicans, socialism, liberals, Baptists, Episcopal. So the message for our people is Isaiah 49:9: “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves.” Come out of that cage.

And Zechariah shows the way out: “by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” The blood of the covenant is Christ dying on the cross. The prisoners are you and me; the pit is Babylon, where there is no water, no truth being taught besides what we are teaching. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: the stronghold is the commandments in the name of Christ. The Christ who preached to the spirits in prison is the one who brings us out of this prison without bars.

precepts.text: For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. A soldier broke it down: you trick yourself into being scared because you make up things in your mind which are not really there. And you also have a lack of faith: your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is only in what you can see with your eyes.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

moments.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

points: For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. Succour means comfort, to run to the rescue, to provide relief in a time of extreme distress. We would choose the easier way out rather than challenge something that causes us to employ discipline, and it is a betraying comfort to do nothing.

Definition read in class: this passage addresses the danger of abandoning logical, structured thought in moments of panic. In times of crisis, fear tempts us to abandon sound judgment for an easier, often false sense of emotional safety. Fear causes us to betray our own capacity for logic, because it feels safer in the moment to panic than to face reality with reason. Sound judgment means making a real effort to correct alcoholic behavior, or doing the disciplined thing to curb the fat, instead of finding an excuse, or a scripture to abuse so you can say the Bible told me I could do this.

Document read in class: the 1883 letter of King Leopold II of Belgium to the colonial missionaries being sent into the Congo. Your principal objective is never to teach the Africans to know God, for this they know already; your essential role is to facilitate the task of administrators and industrials, and interpret the gospel the way that will best protect your interests. Keep watch on disinteresting the people from the richness that is plenty in their underground, lest they dream one day to overthrow you. Find texts encouraging your followers to love poverty, like happier are the poor, for they will inherit heaven. Make them disrespect everything which gives courage to affront us. Direct your action essentially to the younger ones, so the children learn to obey the missionary rather than their parents. Insist on total submission and obedience. And: teach students to read and not to reason.

Teach them to read but not to reason: up to this point many of us did not think there was a difference between the two. Definition read in class: reasoning is the cognitive process of using existing knowledge, facts, and logic to draw conclusions, make decisions, or solve problems; it bridges the gap between raw information and rational action, allowing you to move from one idea to a related idea. Our colonizers do not want us to have this ability, because reasoning is work: the mental work of sitting down, organizing, assessing, the work of a manager, an organizer, a builder.

This is what the stewardship program was: we canvassed the congregation to find out who knew what, who was skilled where, and organized the doctors, nurses, lawyers, paralegals, engineers, electricians, and building specialists into the pie chart. The reasonable solutions were available, right around us; we did not have to go out into the world to get them. That is not selling out; that is organizing exactly what the definition said, and now when people come in with problems, we meet problems with solutions, like Hope and Healing and the doula program. Real people are getting real help because an organizational effort was made.

Because of our inability to reason, we become frustrated and flustered in our thoughts. We know we should do things, but because we are not educated as a collective to reason and organize the elements around us, we act like we cannot, we begin to believe we cannot, and we are frustrated. There is a danger in not reasoning; that is why Leopold said do not teach them to reason, because if they ever learn, we are in trouble.

Example of the fear that runs from reasoning: the fear of acknowledging boldly the black Christ of the Holy Bible. Family members in the church will tell you to get that Bible away from them rather than read what is written. Because of this fear we seek a false and betraying comfort, a cognitive dissonance that normalizes sedative behavior and leaves us comfortably numb in our non-productivity. We say the color of Christ does not matter. Reasoning, if actually applied, would cause us to lay out the elements of our immediate existence and envision a solution to our problems; instead we look for excuses to be docile, for alcohol and getting drunk.

News video played in class: South African leader Julius Malema, long targeted by the AfriForum lobby over the liberation chant a court had ruled protected political speech, was sentenced to prison, and the video connected AfriForum's lobbying of the American administration to aid cuts projected to cost hundreds of thousands of lives. The nations protect the economic inequality apartheid built, and a white minority that lost political control used foreign power to punish a nation into submission. What is happening to our people in South Africa is connected to us from Soweto to Harlem: a collective exploitation of us all. Like Malcolm said, four fifths of the world is not white; they hold it by making us think we are all different while they pillage everybody.

Video played in class: an economist stating plainly that sub-Saharan Africa has been fundamental to global prosperity as a raw material producer, that the economic structures and institutions are designed to keep Africa impoverished, and that whether it is Europe, the US, or China, they need those materials dirt cheap. That is reality, and it can look insurmountable. You cannot get weak and say the order is fixed. Get that thinking out of your mind: we have God behind us, and with God behind us there is no doubt.

So because we feel trapped in so many psychological problems, and feel we could never solve them, we resort to the bottle, to drugs, to promiscuity, to domestic violence and misplaced aggression that affects our youth. Rather than reasoning with your brothers, we turn to violence against those closest to us. And alcohol itself is a huge influence toward violence and self destruction; that is why it is readily available to our people. We use the excuse that we are ready to perish as a reason to feed the disease. If our ancestors had used that excuse to get drunk, none of us would be here today.
